Run Number
EMS-2024-03318
DISPATCH INFORMATION
Unit dispatched Priority 2 to eastbound Route 9 near mile marker 14 for reported two-vehicle motor vehicle collision with one restrained occupant complaining of neck and back pain. Law enforcement on scene prior to arrival.
SCENE FINDINGS
On arrival crew found a 2018 sedan with moderate rear-end deformity, rear bumper and trunk intrusion approximately 18 inches.
Airbags did not deploy. Patient was the restrained driver, self-extricated prior to EMS arrival, and was ambulatory at the roadside.
Second vehicle (pickup truck) with front-end damage; that driver refused transport.
PATIENT ASSESSMENT
Patient is a 36-year-old male, alert and oriented x4, GCS 15. Complains of immediate onset posterior neck pain, mid and lower back pain, and a 'jolt' sensation down the right leg. Denies loss of consciousness, denies head strike, denies chest pain, denies shortness of breath, denies abdominal pain. No numbness in upper extremities. Ambulatory but reports pain with weight bearing on the right.
Airway patent. Breath sounds clear and equal bilaterally. Skin warm and dry. Pupils equal, round, reactive. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Pelvis stable. No obvious deformity, no external hemorrhage. Cervical midline tenderness present at approximately C5-C6 level. Lumbar paraspinal tenderness present bilaterally, greater on the right.
VITAL SIGNS
17: 56
BP 148/88, HR 96, RR 20, SpO2 98% RA, Pain 7/10 18: 12
BP 141/84, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 99% RA, Pain 7/10
TREATMENT RENDERED
– Full spinal motion restriction applied: rigid cervical collar, scoop stretcher transfer
– Oxygen not required, room air maintained
– IV access deferred, patient stable
– Position of comfort, supine with padding
TRANSPORT
Transported non-emergent to Piedmont County General Hospital. No change in patient condition en route. Report given to ED triage RN at 18: 19. Care transferred without incident.
Crew: J. Okafor, NRP (Lead) / T. Bianchi, EMT-B. Report electronically signed 02/11/2024 19: 40.

PIEDMONT COUNTY GENERAL HOSPITAL
Department of Emergency Medicine
EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN NOTE
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. MRN PCG-4471902
Date of Service
02/11/2024
Attending S. Nakamura, MD, FACEP
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Neck and low back pain following motor vehicle collision.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 36-year-old male with no significant past medical history who presents by EMS following a motor vehicle collision that occurred earlier this evening. He reports he was stopped at a traffic signal when his vehicle was struck from behind by a pickup truck. He was restrained by a three-point harness. Airbags did not deploy. He denies striking his head, denies loss of consciousness, and denies any period of confusion.
He describes immediate onset of posterior neck pain, non-radiating, rated 6/10, and low back pain rated 8/10 which radiates into the right buttock and down the posterior right thigh to approximately the level of the knee. He describes an associated 'electric' sensation with certain movements. He denies bowel or bladder incontinence, denies saddle anesthesia, denies fever, and denies prior similar symptoms. He states he has never had back problems before and has never been treated for back pain.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Unremarkable per patient report. No prior surgeries. No chronic medications.
ALLERGIES
Codeine - rash.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-developed male, uncomfortable but in no acute distress.
HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. No scalp hematoma. EOMI, PERRL.
Neck: Midline cervical tenderness at C5-C6. No step-off, no crepitus. Range of motion reduced in all planes secondary to pain and guarding.
Chest/CV: Clear to auscultation. Regular rate and rhythm. No chest wall tenderness, no seatbelt sign.
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended, non-tender.
Back: Lumbar paraspinal muscle spasm palpable bilaterally, more pronounced on the right. Tenderness at L4-L5 and L5-S1 levels.
No midline step-off.
Neuro: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Motor 5/5 throughout except right hip flexion and great toe extension limited to 4+/5, effort-limited by pain. Sensation intact. Deep tendon reflexes 2+ and symmetric at patella and Achilles. Straight leg raise positive on the right at approximately 45 degrees, negative on the left.
MEDICAL DECISION MAKING
Given midline cervical tenderness with a distracting injury, NEXUS criteria are not satisfied and CT cervical spine was obtained.
Lumbar radiographs obtained given focal tenderness and radicular complaints. Imaging reviewed independently by me and is without acute traumatic finding, as detailed in the radiology reports. Neurologic examination is non-focal apart from pain-limited effort. No red flag features for cauda equina.
Working impression is acute cervical strain and acute lumbosacral strain with right-sided radicular symptoms following motor vehicle collision. Discussed conservative management, red flag return precautions, and outpatient follow-up.
DIAGNOSES
1. Cervical strain, acute, initial encounter (S13.4XXA)
2. Lumbosacral strain, acute, initial encounter (S33.5XXA)
3. Radiculopathy, lumbar region, right (M54.41)
4. Motor vehicle collision, occupant, initial encounter (V49.9XXA)
Electronically signed: Sara Nakamura, MD | 02/11/2024 22: 31

DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING REPORTS
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. MRN PCG-4471902
Date of Service
02/11/2024
EXAM 1: CT CERVICAL SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Accession: CT-24-118844 | Performed 19: 48 | CPT 72125 INDICATION: Motor vehicle collision with midline cervical tenderness.
TECHNIQUE: Helical axial images obtained from the skull base through T1 with sagittal and coronal reformations. No intravenous contrast.
FINDINGS: Vertebral body heights are maintained. Alignment is anatomic with preservation of the anterior and posterior vertebral lines. No acute fracture is identified. Facet joints are congruent bilaterally. Mild disc space narrowing at C5-C6 with small anterior osteophyte formation, degenerative in nature. Prevertebral soft tissues are within normal limits. Visualized lung apices are clear.
IMPRESSION:
1. No acute fracture or traumatic malalignment of the cervical spine.
2. Mild degenerative disc disease at C5-C6, chronic.
Reported by: A. Ramachandran, MD | Signed 02/11/2024 20: 22
EXAM 2: RADIOGRAPHS LUMBAR SPINE, 3 VIEWS
Accession: XR-24-118851 | Performed 20: 05 | CPT 72100 INDICATION: Low back pain following motor vehicle collision.
TECHNIQUE: AP, lateral, and spot lateral views of the lumbar spine.
FINDINGS: Five non-rib-bearing lumbar vertebrae. Vertebral body heights preserved without compression deformity. No spondylolisthesis on the lateral view. Mild disc space narrowing at L4-L5 with endplate sclerosis. Facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1, mild to moderate. Sacroiliac joints unremarkable. No acute fracture.
IMPRESSION:
1. No acute fracture or listhesis.
2. Degenerative disc disease and facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1. These findings are chronic and of longstanding duration.
3. Clinical correlation recommended. MRI may be considered if radicular symptoms persist.
Reported by: A. Ramachandran, MD | Signed 02/11/2024 20: 44

ED DISCHARGE SUMMARY & PRESCRIPTION RECORD
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. MRN PCG-4471902
Discharge Date / Time 02/11/2024 21: 52
Disposition Home, ambulatory, accompanied by spouse Condition at Discharge Stable, improved
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES
Acute cervical strain; acute lumbosacral strain; right lumbar radiculopathy; motor vehicle collision.
PRESCRIPTIONS ISSUED
1 Naproxen 500 mg PO BID with food, #30, no refills 2 Methocarbamol 750 mg PO TID PRN muscle spasm, #30, no refills 3 Acetaminophen with Codeine 300/30 mg, 1 tab PO q6h PRN severe pain, #12, no refills
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS
– Apply ice to the neck and low back for 20 minutes every 2-3 hours for the first 48 hours, then may transition to heat.
– Remain as active as tolerated. Avoid bed rest beyond 1-2 days. Avoid lifting greater than 10 pounds for one week.
– Work status: OFF WORK 02/12/2024 through 02/16/2024. May return to light duty 02/19/2024 with no lifting over 15 pounds.
– Follow up with primary care physician within 5-7 days.
– Follow up with orthopedic spine specialist if radicular symptoms persist beyond two weeks.
RETURN PRECAUTIONS - RETURN IMMEDIATELY IF
– Weakness in the legs, difficulty walking, or worsening numbness
– Loss of bowel or bladder control, or numbness in the groin or inner thighs
– Fever, chills, or unrelenting night pain
– Severe headache, vomiting, confusion, or visual change
Patient and spouse verbalized understanding of all instructions, prescriptions, and return precautions. All questions answered.
Written materials provided.

OFFICE VISIT NOTE - PRIMARY CARE
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. DOB 03/14/1987
Date of Service
02/19/2024
Provider L. Osei-Bonsu, MD
Visit Type Follow-up, post motor vehicle collision
SUBJECTIVE
Patient returns 8 days after a rear-end motor vehicle collision on 02/11/2024 for which he was evaluated in the emergency department. He reports neck pain has improved from 6/10 to roughly 3/10 and is now intermittent. Low back pain persists at 6-7/10 and is worse in the morning and after prolonged sitting. Right leg pain continues into the posterior thigh and now extends intermittently to the lateral calf. He reports occasional tingling in the right foot, particularly the top of the foot.
He took the acetaminophen-codeine tablets for two days and stopped, reporting an itchy rash across the chest and forearms which resolved after discontinuation. He continues naproxen with partial benefit. He has not returned to work; he states his employer will not accommodate the light duty restriction at present.
Of note, the patient reports on further questioning that he was involved in a prior rear-end collision in 2021 and had 'a few weeks of back trouble' at that time which resolved without formal treatment. He also recalls being seen at an urgent care for back pain 'a few years ago' but does not recall details.
OBJECTIVE
Vitals: BP 128/80, HR 76, T 98.3F, Wt 194 lb, Ht 5'10", BMI 27.8 General: Well appearing, moves stiffly from seated to standing.
Neck: Mild paraspinal tenderness, full range of motion with end-range discomfort. Spurling maneuver negative bilaterally.
Back: Lumbar flexion limited to approximately 50 degrees by pain. Paraspinal spasm right greater than left. Tenderness over the right L5-S1 facet region.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 except right extensor hallucis longus 4/5. Sensation decreased to light touch over the right L5 dermatome.
Patellar reflexes 2+ bilaterally, Achilles 2+ on the left and 1+ on the right. Straight leg raise positive right at 40 degrees. Crossed straight leg raise negative.
ASSESSMENT
1. Lumbar radiculopathy, right, likely L5 distribution, persistent and not improving at 8 days post-injury.
2. Cervical strain, improving.
3. Adverse drug reaction to codeine - documented allergy, patient was nonetheless prescribed a codeine-containing analgesic at
discharge. Reaction reviewed with patient; codeine added prominently to the chart allergy list.
PLAN
– Discontinue acetaminophen-codeine. Do not re-prescribe any codeine-containing product.
– Continue naproxen 500 mg BID with food. Add gabapentin 300 mg at bedtime, titrate as tolerated.
– Referral to physical therapy, 2 visits per week for 6 weeks.
– Referral to orthopedic spine surgery, Dr. Halloway.
– MRI lumbar spine without contrast ordered given persistent radicular deficit.
– Work note provided: off work through 03/04/2024, reassess.
Electronically signed: Lydia Osei-Bonsu, MD | 02/19/2024 16: 12

VALLEY IMAGING PARTNERS
Advanced Diagnostic Imaging | 1.5T MRI Suite
MRI LUMBAR SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D.
DOB
03/14/1987 Date of Exam
03/06/2024
Accession
MR-24-20719 CPT 72148
Referring L. Osei-Bonsu, MD
CLINICAL HISTORY
36-year-old male, motor vehicle collision 02/11/2024. Persistent right lower extremity radicular pain with L5 sensory deficit and mild weakness. Evaluate for disc herniation.
TECHNIQUE
Multiplanar, multisequence imaging of the lumbar spine performed without intravenous contrast. Sagittal T1, sagittal T2, sagittal STIR, and axial T2 sequences obtained from T12 through S1.
COMPARISON
Lumbar radiographs dated 02/11/2024. No prior cross-sectional imaging available for comparison at this institution.
FINDINGS
Alignment: Normal lumbar alignment. No spondylolisthesis.
Vertebrae: Vertebral body heights and marrow signal are normal. No marrow edema on STIR to suggest acute osseous injury. No compression deformity.
Conus medullaris terminates at the L1 level and is normal in signal.
T12-L1 through L3-L4: No significant disc bulge, herniation, or stenosis. Facets unremarkable.
L4-L5: Moderate disc desiccation with loss of disc height. Broad-based disc bulge with a superimposed RIGHT PARACENTRAL DISC PROTRUSION measuring approximately 6 mm in AP dimension, extending into the right lateral recess. There is contact with and mild posterior displacement of the traversing right L5 nerve root. Mild bilateral facet hypertrophy and ligamentum flavum thickening. Resulting mild to moderate right lateral recess stenosis. Central canal is patent. Neural foramina mildly narrowed on the right.
L5-S1: Disc desiccation with mild loss of height. Small central disc bulge without focal herniation. Moderate bilateral facet arthropathy with periarticular sclerosis. No significant stenosis. Neural foramina patent bilaterally.
Paraspinal soft tissues: Unremarkable. No hematoma or edema.
IMPRESSION
1. L4-L5 right paracentral disc protrusion measuring 6 mm with contact and mild displacement of the traversing right L5 nerve root
and mild to moderate right lateral recess stenosis. This finding correlates with the reported right L5 radicular symptoms.
2. Multilevel degenerative disc disease at L4-L5 and L5-S1 with facet arthropathy. Disc desiccation and facet changes are chronic
and predate the reported injury; the superimposed focal protrusion cannot be dated by imaging alone.
3. No acute fracture, marrow edema, or ligamentous injury.
Reported by: Anand Ramchandran, MD | Electronically signed 03/06/2024 15: 03

HALLOWAY ORTHOPEDIC SPINE INSTITUTE
Spine Surgery and Non-Operative Spine Care
ORTHOPEDIC SPINE CONSULTATION
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. DOB 03/14/1987
Date of Service
03/14/2024
Provider G. Halloway, MD, Orthopedic Spine Surgery
Referral Source L. Osei-Bonsu, MD
HISTORY
This is a 36-year-old right-hand-dominant male warehouse logistics coordinator referred for evaluation of persistent right lower extremity radicular pain following a rear-end motor vehicle collision on 02/11/2024. He was evaluated in the emergency department on the date of injury with negative radiographs. Symptoms have persisted for five weeks despite naproxen, gabapentin, methocarbamol, and six sessions of physical therapy.
He describes low back pain of 5/10 and right leg pain of 7/10, the leg pain now dominant. Pain radiates from the right buttock through the posterolateral thigh and calf into the dorsum of the right foot. He reports numbness over the dorsum of the right foot and a sense that the right foot 'catches' when he is tired. He denies left leg symptoms, denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, and denies saddle anesthesia.
He remains off work. He rates his function as markedly limited and reports inability to sit through a full meal or drive more than 20 minutes.
REVIEW OF PRIOR RECORDS
I have personally reviewed the ED records of 02/11/2024, the lumbar radiographs of the same date, and the MRI lumbar spine of 03/06/2024. I have also reviewed the cervical spine MRI dated 03/2024 which demonstrates no significant cord compression.
Physical therapy notes reviewed.
EXAMINATION
Gait antalgic on the right. Heel walking on the right is weak; toe walking intact. Lumbar flexion to 50 degrees, extension to 15 degrees with reproduction of leg pain.
Motor: Right EHL 4/5. Right tibialis anterior 4+/5. Right gastrocnemius 5/5. Left lower extremity 5/5 throughout. Hip abduction symmetric.
Sensory: Diminished pinprick right L5 dermatome, dorsum of foot and lateral calf.
Reflexes: Patellar 2+ bilaterally. Achilles 2+ left, 1+ right.
Provocative: Right straight leg raise positive at 35 degrees reproducing leg pain. Contralateral SLR negative. FABER negative bilaterally. No hip joint pain with internal rotation.
ASSESSMENT
Right L5 radiculopathy secondary to an L4-L5 right paracentral disc protrusion, symptomatic and correlating with imaging.
Underlying multilevel degenerative disc disease is present and is chronic; in my opinion the acute focal protrusion and the onset of radicular symptoms are temporally related to the collision of 02/11/2024, in a spine with pre-existing degenerative change that was asymptomatic prior to the event.
PLAN
1. Continue physical therapy, extend authorization by 4 weeks.
2. Referral to interventional pain management for right L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection.
3. Continue gabapentin, titrate to 300 mg TID.
4. Repeat evaluation in 6 weeks. If radicular pain and EHL weakness persist despite injection, would discuss right L4-L5
microdiscectomy.
5. Work status: remains off work.
Electronically signed: Gregory Halloway, MD | 03/14/2024

SUMMIT INTERVENTIONAL PAIN & SPINE
Ambulatory Procedure Suite | Fluoroscopy Room 2
PROCEDURE NOTE - TRANSFORAMINAL EPIDURAL STEROID INJECTION
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. DOB 03/14/1987 Date of Procedure
04/23/2024
Proceduralist D. Farhadi, MD Pre-procedure Diagnosis Right L5 radiculopathy, L4-L5 disc protrusion Post-procedure Diagnosis
Same
Procedure Right L5-S1 transforaminal epidural steroid injection under fluoroscopic guidance (CPT 64483)
Anesthesia Local, 1% lidocaine. No sedation.
Complications
None
INDICATION
Patient with imaging-confirmed right paracentral L4-L5 disc protrusion and clinically corroborated right L5 radiculopathy, refractory to eight weeks of oral medication and fourteen sessions of physical therapy. Risks, benefits, and alternatives including continued conservative care and surgical decompression were discussed. Written informed consent obtained.
TECHNIQUE
Patient placed prone on the fluoroscopy table with a bolster beneath the abdomen. The lumbosacral region was prepped with chlorhexidine and draped in sterile fashion. Under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance the target foramen was identified and the C-arm obliqued to visualize the 'Scotty dog' view. Skin and subcutaneous tissue infiltrated with 1% lidocaine.
A 22-gauge spinal needle was advanced under intermittent fluoroscopy to the safe triangle beneath the pedicle. Position confirmed on AP and lateral views. Negative aspiration for blood and cerebrospinal fluid. Omnipaque 180 contrast, 1 mL, injected demonstrating appropriate epidural and perineural spread along the nerve root without vascular uptake.
A solution of dexamethasone 10 mg with 1 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine was then injected slowly. The patient tolerated the injection well and reported his typical radicular pain reproduced on contrast injection, then relieved.
POST-PROCEDURE
Patient monitored in recovery for 30 minutes. Motor and sensory function intact bilaterally. Ambulated without difficulty.
Discharged home in stable condition with a responsible adult driver.
Pre-procedure pain 7/10. Immediate post-procedure pain 2/10 (anesthetic phase).
PLAN
– Pain diary for 14 days.
– Resume physical therapy in 3 days.
– Follow up in 3 weeks. May consider a second injection if partial but incomplete relief.
– Return to Dr. Halloway if relief is inadequate to discuss surgical options.

EMG / NERVE CONDUCTION STUDY REPORT
Patient Whitfield, Marcus D. DOB 03/14/1987 Date of Study

CLINICAL INDICATION

Anesthesia General endotracheal, administered by V. Sokolova, MD
Estimated Blood Loss 25 mL
Specimens Disc material, sent to pathology

None
PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS
Right L4-L5 herniated nucleus pulposus with right L5 radiculopathy, failed conservative management.
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS
Same, confirmed intraoperatively.
PROCEDURE PERFORMED
Right L4-L5 hemilaminotomy with microdiscectomy and decompression of the right L5 nerve root (CPT 63030).
INDICATIONS
The patient is a 37-year-old male with a right L4-L5 disc protrusion causing right L5 radiculopathy with motor deficit, which has failed a course of physical therapy, oral neuropathic and anti-inflammatory medication, and one transforaminal epidural steroid injection. Symptoms have persisted for approximately seven months. Risks, benefits, and alternatives were reviewed and informed consent obtained.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE
The patient was brought to the operating room and general anesthesia was induced without difficulty. He was turned prone onto a Wilson frame with all pressure points padded. A surgical time-out was performed confirming patient identity, procedure, and correct operative level and laterality.
The lumbar region was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. A localizing radiograph confirmed the L4-L5 interspace. A midline incision was made and carried through subcutaneous tissue. Subperiosteal dissection was carried out on the right side exposing the L4 lamina and L4-L5 interlaminar space. A retractor was placed and a repeat radiograph confirmed the level.
Using the operating microscope, a hemilaminotomy of the inferior margin of the right L4 lamina was performed with a high-speed burr and Kerrison rongeurs. The ligamentum flavum was incised and removed. The thecal sac and traversing right L5 nerve root were identified. The nerve root was noted to be tented and erythematous over a firm extruded disc fragment in the right lateral recess.
The nerve root was gently retracted medially. The fragment was delivered with a pituitary rongeur and additional loose degenerative nucleus pulposus was removed from the disc space. The lateral recess and foramen were then probed and found to be widely decompressed. The nerve root was noted to be freely mobile.
Hemostasis was obtained with bipolar cautery and thrombin-soaked Gelfoam. The wound was irrigated with antibiotic solution.
The fascia was closed with 0-Vicryl, subcutaneous tissue with 2-0 Vicryl, and skin with a running subcuticular 4-0 Monocryl. A sterile dressing was applied. All counts were correct. The patient was awakened, extubated, and transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit in stable condition.
